subject: EdgeApps token-savings sprint: batching, prefetch, quant profiles
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@edgeapps.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeApps token-savings sprint: batching, prefetch, quant profiles

Hi Anna —

Great to meet you on the call today. As discussed, we can run a focused two-week "token-savings sprint" to lock in safe cost reductions for your core generation path without impacting latency objectives. High-level proposal: 

- Week 0 (prep): collect latency/cost baseline + traffic slices, pick primary prompt families.
- Week 1: enable prefix/KV prefetch for the 3 heaviest prompt families + batch sizing tweaks.
- Week 2: evaluate 8-bit quant profile candidates and routing fallbacks to a cheaper variant for low-SLO workloads.

Immediate asks for your team so we can schedule work:
1) Attach a ~48-hour traffic sample or a link to the query slice (we'll use the template attached).
2) Confirm the two SLOs to target (p50 / p95 latencies in ms) and the acceptable quality delta threshold (e.g., <=1% change in top-1 accuracy).

I'll loop Monica for measurement and Vivek for quant routing notes. Proposed kickoff: Monday 19 May, 10am PT. Let me know if that works.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: token_savings_template.xlsx

From: Anna Park <anna@edgeapps.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeApps token-savings sprint: batching, prefetch, quant profiles

Thanks Jonas — this sounds good. A few quick clarifications: 

- We can provide a 72-hour sample from our production ingestion; will drop it in the Drive link tonight.
- Our internal SRE wants to keep p95 under 380ms for the primary route; p50 target 90ms.
- Quality tolerance: product wants <0.5% end-user visible regressions (we have automated evals for the prompt families).

Kickoff Monday 19th 10am PT works for me and I'll invite our SRE lead (cc below).

Anna Park
Head of Product
EdgeApps

Cc: EdgeApps - SRE Team <sre@edgeapps.ai>

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Anna Park <anna@edgeapps.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeApps token-savings sprint: batching, prefetch, quant profiles

Thanks Anna — quick operational checklist from engineering measurement side so the sprint is productive: 

1) Data & slices: we need the sample as CSV with these columns: timestamp, route, prompt_family, input_len, output_len, model_variant, region. The template Jonas attached will map those.
2) Baseline traces: a production p95/p99 sample and a flamegraph snapshot if possible (latency_baseline.png helps).
3) Test harness: share your automated eval harness or a short list of prompt->expected outputs so we can run regression checks post-quant.

On the tech plan side I'll lead: 
- Day 1-2: run offline batching simulator across sample to choose target batch sizes (aim to maximize GPU fill while keeping tail latency).
- Day 3-6: enable prefix/KV caching for the top 2 prompt families and measure hit rates.
- Day 7-10: candidate quant profiles (8-bit symmetric + 6-bit mixed) on a dev replica and run evals.
- Day 11-12: deployment plan for safe gradual rollout + routing rule to fall back to the high-precision variant if quality or latency regressions are detected.

I'll upload a quant_profile_matrix.pdf with candidate profiles and expected token savings.

Monica Patel
Technical Success Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: quant_profile_matrix.pdf

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@edgeapps.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeApps token-savings sprint: batching, prefetch, quant profiles

Anna / team — adding a short routing and fallback note so the SREs can review before kickoff: 

- Routing policy: primary route -> quantized-optimized variant (Q8) for small-medium seqs; fallback route -> FP16 high-precision for specific customer payloads or when the model confidence delta > threshold.
- Health checks: measure rolling 1min error-rate and 5min p95 latency; if either breaches set thresholds we immediately signal an automatic rollback.
- Canary cadence: 5% -> 20% -> 60% over 4 hours with automated regression checks at each step.

Laura — can you prepare the runbook snippet for the SRE team (short checklist for rollback commands + where KV cache metrics appear in Console)?

Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Anna Park <anna@edgeapps.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeApps token-savings sprint: batching, prefetch, quant profiles

Anna — attaching the lightweight SRE runbook as discussed. Key excerpts below:

1) Quick rollback: `redwood rollback --route edgeapps-primary --to fp16-2025-05-01` (takes ~2m to propagate).
2) KV cache keys: Console -> Routes -> edgeapps-primary -> Cache metrics. Hit rate >= 40% is a good early signal.
3) Batch tuning: start at 4 tokens/slot and run the sampler for 30 minutes; if p95 increases >10% revert to previous batch size.
4) Post-quant validation: run the supplied eval harness (link above). If >0.5% top-1 delta on any key prompt family abort and rollback.

We'll bring the attachments into the kickoff doc and share the Drive folder link in the invite. Looking forward to Monday.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: latency_baseline.png
